rationale: X's 'Validated' bullets directly engage the exact code paths the human reviewers flagged — talker fail-fast for library callers, shared duration-factor constants across adapter/talker/s2mel, and native-speed streaming gating (HTTP fixed, WebSocket still requires speed=1.0) — confirming those concerns were addressed, plus it surfaces well-evidenced novel findings (unmarked pytest files silently deselected by CI markers, Spanish TN silently degrading to identity). Y is well-written and technically careful with several plausible latent bugs (uninitialized mel_head.bias, tensor-concat accumulation hazard, CPU snapshot no-copy), but none of its findings overlap with what the actual reviewers raised, so it covers almost none of the ground-truth concern set. Both reviews are comparably grounded and actionable with concrete file/line evidence and explicit suggested changes, but X's substantially higher recall of the real reviewer concerns decides it.
